$comment: THE SURVIVOR BAND BY LADDER POSITION — how many of the configurations a scenario's survivor count judged may get through, by where the scenario sits on data/campaign.json's ordered path. GitHub issue #234, DECISIONS.md § D537, the product owner's ruling of 2026-09-10 (quoted in provenance.ruling). ITS ONLY READER is packages/viz/src/scenario/survivorBands.test.ts, through survivorBands.test-helper.ts: an acceptance check on data/scenario-survivors.json, on the footing docs/33 DC-4's [1/3, 2/3] band stands on. No screen, no award and no run reads this file, and the reader is a test helper so that a draft figure cannot reach a shipped path. PROVENANCE, per the product owner's 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values: EVERY FIGURE IN THIS FILE IS AN AGENT'S PROPOSAL, DRAFTED FOR THE OWNER TO ACCEPT, TIGHTEN OR REJECT, and provenance.approval reads 'draft' until the owner says otherwise. The line that ruling asks for falls entirely on one side here. What is MEASURED: nothing in this file. Every survivor, examined, unjudged and suppressed count lives in data/scenario-survivors.json, which is generated and says so, and this file is kept apart from it so that a table of measurements never carries a choice. What is CHOSEN: every position boundary, every share, and the yardstick each note argues from. What is RULED rather than chosen, and therefore enforced by the check rather than authored here: the band narrows down the ladder (the ceiling, the floor and the width may not grow from one band to the next); positions one and two may allow many survivors, because a dropdown clear is permitted there (§ D528); every position allows at least one survivor, which is § D525 clause 3's 'zero is not a scenario' — so a minShare of 0 below does NOT permit zero — and a scenario that declares a diagnosis and has no survivor is exempt from that floor and from nothing else; and no band may admit the whole space, which is DC-1 as a reading of the count. WHAT A SHARE IS A SHARE OF: survivors over the configurations judged at the scenario's BASE budget rung — examined less unjudged, which on the table measured 2026-09-10 is examined itself, because nothing there was unjudged. Suppressed configurations stay in the share and a scenario below its band on which every examined configuration was suppressed is read apart from one below it over measured runs; survivorBands.test-helper.ts's docstring says why each of those is the rule. WHAT THIS BAND CANNOT SEE: which configuration got through. A scenario whose only survivor is a shipped dispatcher profile picked from the dropdown can sit inside its band at position three or later, where § D528 clause 2 says no single profile may meet every bar on its own; that clause is held by packages/viz/src/campaign/difficultyCurve.test.ts's DROPDOWN_CLEARS register and not by this file, so inside a band is not the same claim as rebalanced. A reader disagreeing with a figure here is disagreeing with a judgement, not correcting a measurement, and the lever is one field in this file.

provenance.ruling: The product owner, 2026-09-10, on GitHub issue #234: 'The survivor band narrows by ladder position. Positions 1–2 may allow many survivors, because a dropdown clear is permitted there (§ D528); later positions allow few, but at least one. The band is authored in data as shares of the configurations examined, drafted for approval. The rebalance then moves demand and building fabric, never a bar, to bring each scenario inside its band.' Recorded as DECISIONS.md § D537.

bands.note: CHOSEN: between a quarter and three quarters of the configurations judged get through, for the two scenarios a player meets first. The ruling lets these positions allow many survivors because a dropdown clear is permitted here (§ D528), and the owner's words for the opening are 'doable with tweaks, and failable with the wrong tweaks' (§ D525) and 'it's fine that the first building is hard to fail' (§ D528). The yardstick both edges are argued from: at a share of 0.25, three configurations tried independently find at least one way through with probability 1 − 0.75³ ≈ 0.58, and at 0.75 they meet at least one that fails with the same probability, so a player who tries three things is more likely than not to see both halves. Nobody plays by drawing at random; the yardstick is a way of stating a share a designer can argue with, not a model of play, and its arithmetic has to be redone if either share moves. THE FLOOR IS THE FIGURE MOST WORTH ATTACKING: the ruling sets a ceiling here and names no floor above one survivor, so 0.25 is this draft's reading of 'doable with tweaks' rather than the ruling's own words. The alternative is a minShare of 0, which leaves the floor at the one survivor every position carries — and packages/viz/src/scenario/survivors.ts's first-hour rule, which refuses a count of exactly one in a player's first hour, would then make it two.

CHOSEN: at least one survivor and at most a fifth of the configurations judged. Position three is where § D528 clause 2 ends the opening — a player has met the editor twice — and where the ruling stops allowing many survivors. The yardstick: at 0.20, three configurations tried independently find a way through with probability 1 − 0.8³ ≈ 0.49, so from here three guesses more often than not find nothing, which is #234's own complaint as a figure: a stage cleared by picking from a list teaches nothing. minShare is 0 because the floor is the one survivor § D525 clause 3 sets at every position, enforced by the check rather than written here. On the shipped campaign positions three and four are still inside the derived first hour, where survivors.ts refuses a count of exactly one; this band does not restate that rule, because the first-hour set is derived from the stages' durations rather than their positions and would go stale here the first time a duration moved.

CHOSEN: at least one survivor and at most 0.15 of the configurations judged. The yardstick: at 0.15, four configurations tried independently find a way through with probability 1 − 0.85⁴ ≈ 0.48. The ceiling steps down by 0.05 rather than by more because the table measured on 2026-09-10 judges twenty or twenty-four configurations a scenario, where 0.05 is about one survivor; a finer step would ask for a distinction the count cannot make.

CHOSEN: at least one survivor and at most a tenth of the configurations judged, at position eight and every position after it. The yardstick: at 0.10, six configurations tried independently find a way through with probability 1 − 0.9⁶ ≈ 0.47. Open-ended, so a scenario added to the end of the ladder has a band without an edit. Over the twenty or twenty-four configurations the table judged a scenario on 2026-09-10 this admits one or two survivors, and one is the hardest § D525 clause 3 lets a scenario be.
